results.reason: Issue 1 identifies the Varga stock purchase as a Change of Control under §1.1(a). It says §15.4 requires Crestline's prior written consent and that item 3.4 wrongly says 'notice only; no consent required.' It ties this to a termination right, a termination fee and an inaccurate §3.5 representation.
The response never discusses §14.2, the 'Qualified Transferee' definition, or Crestline's ability to assign the agreement to a Halvorsen competitor without consent.

Issue 6 explains that the First Amendment restates §12.3 to carve out only §9 breaches. It also says §§10 and 11 now fall under the cap, so claims against Crestline are capped. However, it never says the amendment controls under the order-of-precedence clause in §17.5, which the criterion expressly requires.
Issue 6 states that the original §12.3 excluded breaches of §9 or §10 and the indemnification obligations under §11 from the limitations.
The response describes the §12.2 cap as amounts paid or payable to Supplier in the preceding 12 months, and in Issue 7 as amounts paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim.
The memo lists ten separate issues. Each has 'Where it appears' (document and section), 'Why it matters for Halvorsen', and 'Recommended fix' headings.
The response concludes that consent is required and expressly rejects the notice-only classification.
The response states that the First Amendment removed the §10 and §11 carve-outs and that those claims are now capped.
